title: The Autobiography
author: Benjamin Franklin
blurb: How a runaway printer's apprentice became one of history's great persuaders — by never arguing, keeping a little book of virtues, and asking favours.

contradiction.m: Saying the opposite of what someone said.
contradiction.e: Her blunt contradiction annoyed the speaker.

obliged.e: You obliged me by driving me home.

industry.e: Through industry she paid off her loan early.

cards.title: Stop winning arguments
cards.text: As a young man Franklin loved debating and crushing people. He noticed it made enemies. So he switched to asking modest questions instead — and persuaded far more people.
cards.quote: put on the humble inquirer and doubter
cards.qMean: Instead of arguing, ask questions like someone curious.
cards.qLife: 'Have you thought about…?' works better than 'You're wrong.'
cards.cap: Benjamin Franklin as an apprentice · public domain

cards.title: Never say 'you're wrong'
cards.text: Franklin banned himself from flat contradiction and from words like 'certainly'. He said 'I imagine' or 'it appears to me' — and people stopped resisting his ideas.
cards.quote: I made it a rule to forbear all direct contradiction to the sentiments of others, and all positive assertion of my own.
cards.qMean: Don't bluntly contradict people or insist you're right.
cards.qLife: Saying 'I might be wrong, but…' before a suggestion.
cards.cap: Benjamin Franklin at the Court of France · public domain

cards.title: Ask for a favour
cards.text: To win over a hostile rival, Franklin asked to borrow a rare book. The man lent it, and became a lifelong friend. People like those they've helped — now called the 'Ben Franklin effect'.
cards.quote: He that has once done you a kindness will be more ready to do you another, than he whom you yourself have obliged.
cards.qMean: Someone who helped you once is more likely to help again than someone you helped.
cards.qLife: Asking a cold colleague for advice often warms them up.

cards.title: A little book of habits
cards.text: Franklin listed thirteen virtues and kept a small book with a page for each, marking his slips every day. A habit tracker, 250 years early.
cards.quote: I made a little book, in which I allotted a page for each of the virtues.
cards.qMean: He tracked his habits daily in a notebook.
cards.qLife: Ticking off 'no sugar' days on a calendar.

cards.title: Lose no time
cards.text: His sixth virtue, Industry: never waste time, always be doing something useful, and cut out what isn't needed.
cards.quote: Lose no time; be always employ'd in something useful; cut off all unnecessary actions.
cards.qMean: Don't waste time; keep doing useful things.
cards.qLife: Listening to an audiobook during your commute.

cards.title: Speak usefully
cards.text: His second virtue, Silence: only say what helps others or yourself, and skip empty chatter.
cards.quote: Speak not but what may benefit others or yourself; avoid trifling conversation.
cards.qMean: Only say things that are helpful.
cards.qLife: Skipping office gossip and talking about real work.
cards.cap: Christian Schussele - Benjamin Franklin Appearing before the Privy Council · public domain
